references.text: Continuation of the laws on theft and restitution, elaborating on the consequences when a thief is caught
Laws on restitution and guilt offering when someone has acted deceitfully toward their neighbor regarding property
Requirement for full restitution plus one-fifth for sin against other people
David judges that the one who stole a lamb must repay fourfold, in accordance with the law of restitution
Reference to sevenfold restitution for theft, showing how the principle of restitution was applied
The wicked shall restore what they have robbed, as a principle of restoration
Zacchaeus promises to repay fourfold to those he has defrauded, in line with the Mosaic law's principle of restitution
Complementary rules on theft: 21:37 covers slaughtered/sold animals (5x/4x), while 22:3 covers live found animals (double restitution).
Contrast in responsibility: 21:37 punishes deliberate theft with high restitution, while 21:28 distinguishes between guilt and innocence in cases of accidental animal harm.
Thematic parallel in the law of restitution: 21:37 covers animals, while 22:6 extends the principle of double restitution to other stolen items.
